extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark composed of 680 queries from four real-world scenarios (education, conference, organization, and game domains) across over 1373 webpages, designed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website using a Question-Answer format.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing official websites recursively, constructing queries based on page information, and verifying/filtering for legitimate queries. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game), comprising over 1373 webpages. Web page content was collected as markdown content along with clickable HTML buttons extracted using Beautiful Soup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-stage funnel annotation strategy: (1) LLM-based annotation using GPT-4o for initial annotations including query construction, verification, and filtering; (2) crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o used for initial annotations including query construction, verification, and filtering of QA pairs
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently comprises only 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. The benchmark only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons, excluding visual modalities such as screenshots. WebWalker is driven by prompting without additional training. The dataset is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, which pre-trained models cannot access due to static knowledge cutoff dates.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating LLMs' web traversal abilities in complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks. It can be used for benchmarking RAG systems, training/fine-tuning web navigation agents using approximately 14k silver QA pairs as supplementary training data, and testing multi-agent frameworks for web navigation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The WebWalkerQA dataset will be made available on HuggingFace Datasets, and the code for WebWalker will be released on GitHub. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dataset is categorized by difficulty level (easy, medium, hard) based on subpage depth, and includes both single-source and multi-source QA types to simulate different human information-seeking behaviors.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage funnel annotation: (1) GPT-4o performs initial annotation by recursively traversing official websites, constructing queries, and filtering for legitimate QA pairs with short answers containing entities; (2) human annotators rewrite and calibrate questions and answers for correctness and consistency.
